title: Observe requests with injected time
summary: Wrap an http.Handler with timing middleware that buffered the response, reports whole milliseconds, and keeps request context and output intact.
objectives: Wrap an http.Handler with middleware that measures elapsed time through an injected Clock.
Buffer the downstream response so a header can be set before the first byte is flushed.
Preserve downstream status, headers, body, and request context exactly.
constraints: Keep the Clock interface and the Observe(clock Clock, next http.Handler) http.Handler signature.
Call clock.Now() exactly twice per request, before and after the downstream handler.
Never call time.Now, time.Since, or time.Sleep.
Preserve the downstream status code, headers, and body exactly.
Set X-Elapsed-Ms before the response is flushed.
Pass the original request context to the downstream handler.

examples.explanation: Elapsed time is reported in whole milliseconds.

examples.input: before = 10:00:00.000, after = 10:00:00.0004, downstream status 204, empty body
examples.explanation: Milliseconds() truncates, and an empty body stays empty.
The middleware reports time honestly, including failures.

public.name: Bodies are preserved
public.description: Empty and multi-line bodies survive the middleware unchanged.

hidden.name: Context and call count
hidden.description: Request values reach the handler and the clock is called exactly twice.

hidden.name: Error responses
hidden.description: 404, 400, and 500 statuses and bodies are preserved.
